sources.title: FAO1975 — Synopsis of biological data on the Norway lobster
sources.scope: Selected actual PDFpage10 diagnosis and pages12–13 external morphology read; actual Fig1/page11 and Fig2/page14 viewed. Kidney-shaped eye ends, slim unequal ridged chelae, three lateral rostral spine pairs, sculptured serial abdomen and P2/P3 small chelae guide the partial reconstruction. Adult and juvenile claw figures distinguished; historical taxonomy/type/fishery statements are not adopted as current determinations or physiology.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual PDF text and rendered primary figures

sources.title: Naturalis/FAO Marine Lobsters — Nephrops norvegicus
sources.scope: Selected species diagnosis read for unequal longitudinally grooved/ridged chelae, spinulate carinae and sculptured abdominal somites. No measured morphology, optics or dynamics imported.

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A slender ridged carapace, authored kidney-shaped eye ends, three lateral rostral spine pairs with a ventral tooth cue, unequal elongated ridged palms, four pairs of jointed walking limbs with small P2/P3 chelae, six sculptured abdominal plates and a separate five-part fan replace the generic lobster.
shape.remaining: Fine eye contour, rostral variation, spine/denticle positions, setal density, scaphocerite shape, detailed grooves and joints remain approximate. The mild selected abdominal arch does not reproduce every captive/wild posture. First sex-modified pleopods and internal organs are incomplete; the source photo does not independently establish sex or stage.

surface.changed: Dorsal orange and a lighter underside, longitudinal palm/carapace ridge cues, small spine rows and pale serial seam margins are original numerical cuticle surfaces. The selected captive photograph guides the orange/cream appearance without calibrating material properties.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, without calibrated optics, scan or full natural variation. Fine eye contour, rostral variation, spine/denticle positions, setal density, scaphocerite shape, detailed grooves and joints remain approximate. The mild selected abdominal arch does not reproduce every captive/wild posture. First sex-modified pleopods and internal organs are incomplete; the source photo does not independently establish sex or stage.

movement.changed: Short authored forward support, local unequal-chela handling/opening, quiet supported posture with a mild serial abdominal arch, and partial added flex/fan articulation. No burrow digging, swimming escape, feeding, pressure/flow or physiological mechanism is simulated.
movement.remaining: No measured coordinates, natural playback rate, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, muscle, food contact, ingestion, sensory physiology or independent biological validation. Fixed-length/support checks establish internal software consistency only.

sourceAssessment: Hans Hillewaert's authentic Cretaquarium photo was viewed. Selected FAO1975 synopsis diagnosis/external morphology text and actual Figure1/PDF11, Figure2/PDF14 were compared, distinguishing adult unequal chelae from juvenile stages. Naturalis/FAO selected diagnosis was read separately. Historical taxonomy/type-locality statements are not substituted for current accepted species linkage.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Darkened the too-pale first render into a dorsal-orange/light-ventral field.
Added a mild serial resting arch after comparison with the source photograph; checked additional flex for floor clearance.
Kept long grooved unequal palms and five posterior ridge cues distinct from smooth Homarus palms.
Moved the carapace ridge paths onto its curved surface to avoid unsupported lateral ribs.

The full-cycle maximum-flex check caught a brief floor intersection missed by the sparse initial times. Reduced the partial flex range and replaced all affected final tail/detail views before publication.
Bound the three anatomy markers to the carapace, actual crusher palm and moving fan, and corrected the inherited label names.

assessmentRubric.identity: Accepted species-rank concept checked; photographed organism remains source-labelled
assessmentRubric.body: Substantial initial correction; unmeasured dimensions and incomplete fine diagnostic anatomy
assessmentRubric.texture: Distinct selected numerical surface; optics and microanatomy remain illustrative
assessmentRubric.movement: Working qualitative supported articulation; empirical rate/dynamics unvalidated

reviewMethod: 55 actual final nonblank side/front/top, enlarged and action/posture states inspected individually on labelled sheets against the authentic photograph and scoped sources. Superseded frames excluded. Qualitative author assessment, not independent expert certification.

samples.status: Actual final frame visually inspected on labelled comparison sheets; qualitative author assessment
samples.finding: A slender ridged carapace, authored kidney-shaped eye ends, three lateral rostral spine pairs with a ventral tooth cue, unequal elongated ridged palms, four pairs of jointed walking limbs with small P2/P3 chelae, six sculptured abdominal plates and a separate five-part fan replace the generic lobster. Dorsal orange and a lighter underside, longitudinal palm/carapace ridge cues, small spine rows and pale serial seam margins are original numerical cuticle surfaces. The selected captive photograph guides the orange/cream appearance without calibrating material properties. Remaining: Fine eye contour, rostral variation, spine/denticle positions, setal density, scaphocerite shape, detailed grooves and joints remain approximate. The mild selected abdominal arch does not reproduce every captive/wild posture. First sex-modified pleopods and internal organs are incomplete; the source photo does not independently establish sex or stage.
